items.summary:
Don’t let your portfolio outsmart you.

If AI helped build your project, be ready to explain the code in an interview. 

Start with one failure case, like a user requesting someone else’s private data. 

Have the agent write a test that expects access to be denied, check that expectation yourself, then review the implementation it produces. #short

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Is AI Changing Software Engineering Forever? GoTo India's Senior Director Explains
items.summary:
In 2020, LogMeIn was taken off the public markets in a massive $4.3 billion private equity buyout. Two years later, it rebranded entirely as GoTo. Today, amidst reports of book net worth dropping over 16% and increasing margin pressure, GoTo’s India engineering base in Bangalore is quietly building a meaningful share of the company's core products.

In this episode of Front Page, Aparna Balasubramanian, Senior Director of Software Engineering at GoTo, sits down to discuss what it’s actually like to lead an engineering team through intense corporate shifts and the messy reality of the AI coding revolution.

items.title: The Hidden Cost of an AI That Never Sleeps
items.summary: In episode 1027 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Dr. Dilani Kahawala, Co-Founder and CEO of Anna, about what it really takes to run an AI assistant on a $20-a-month subscription. She explains why the team shifted toward open-source models as serving their users grew expensive, and why they won't cap a family's usage, working behind the scenes to get the most powerful models for the price.

items.summary:

items.summary:
Welcome to Front Page Live by AIM Network. In today’s broadcast, we break down the most critical shifts happening across global AI, deep-tech, and semiconductor supply chains.

Today's Rundown:
Meta Puts Premium AI Behind a Paywall: Mark Zuckerberg is officially monetizing generative AI. We break down the new "Meta One" subscription tiers—ranging from ₹549 to a massive ₹20,990 per month—and what it means for creators and businesses.

To counter hardware limitations, Huawei is using its proprietary UnifiedBus technology to link up to 1 million processors into massive AI "superclusters," matching the output of top-tier Nvidia GPUs.

items.title: BREAKING: Not Your Normal Microchip! How Odisha Is Building India’s Silicon Carbide Hub
items.summary:
Odisha is securing its spot on India's high-tech manufacturing map! The Falta SEZ Committee approved a ₹3,406.25-crore semiconductor facility for SiCSem at Infovalley-II in Khordha district.

Rather than standard computer processors, this plant will produce Silicon Carbide (SiC) diodes and MOSFETs—critical power semiconductors used in electric vehicles, solar inverters, high-speed rail, and defence systems.

items.title: ALERT: AI Agents Writing 35% of Code While Senior Devs Get 19% Slower | Point Break
items.summary:
Are autonomous agents ending manual coding? We analyze if AI is replacing developers or just building faster software factories.

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Sakshi Jain, Director of Engineering at Harness, and Nagendra Bangalore, Director of Engineering for watsonx Orchestrate at IBM. They explore developer productivity realities across Indian enterprises, automated PR reviews using Harness AI, avoiding AI slop and context rot, separating agent roles between generation and verification, the evolving value of system architects, and how young engineers must preserve critical thinking skills in an agent-driven ecosystem. 

This shift raises critical questions about the future of software engineering and overall AI productivity. Instead of total replacement, we examine whether we are witnessing the rise of high-speed software factories that move faster than humans can track, and what this means for the daily workflow of developers.

items.summary_html:
New data reveals how AI coding tools impact developer speed. Learn why productivity results flipped from a 19% slowdown to an 18% gain.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Nagendra Bangalore, Director of Engineering for watsonx Orchestrate at IBM, whose PhD research examines the evolving relationship between humans and AI across personal and workplace settings. They discuss real-world developer productivity metrics using IBM Bob, maintaining critical thinking while leveraging AI coders, deploying agentic workflows across HR and procurement, building sovereign AI infrastructure with Yotta and Sarvam AI, and establishing evaluation guardrails for enterprise deployment. 

Less than a year later, a follow-up analysis showed a complete reversal, with developers recording an 18% speed increase. We analyze this shift in software engineering and what it means for how teams manage AI productivity in real-world environments.

CHAPTERS:
0:00 The AI Coding Paradox
1:41 Human-AI Relationships and Their Mechanisms
3:59 Defining the Boundaries of AI Dependency
8:05 Inside IBM's AI Coding Philosophy
16:05 Advice for the Next Generation of Engineers
23:46 Are Enterprises Truly Ready for Agentic AI?
43:07 The Fear of Recursive Self-Improvement
